summary: Soft 429s during mixed scheduled batch import and live streaming after proxy rotation - refill window skew
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightRetail reports transient 429 responses for a subset of requests during their nightly scheduled bulk embedding import that runs concurrently with low-latency streaming traffic. The pattern started after a scheduled proxy rotation and persisted intermittently for ~45 minutes.

Impact:
- ~8% of streaming sessions observed soft 429s (short-lived, retriable) causing perceptible latency spikes in downstream application metrics.
- Bulk import workers experienced uneven progress (many small retries), increasing total run time and bumping CPU on ingest nodes.
- Customer is on a Dedicated pool; business impact: degraded storefront personalization during peak morning traffic window.

Environment:
- Customer tier: dedicated
- Pool: dp-us-east-02 (pinned throughput profile)
- Edge proxies behind ALB (rolling rotation at 02:00 UTC)
- Time of events: 2026-03-10 02:03--02:48 UTC

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Start long-running bulk embedding import (multipart parallel upload, 200 workers, staggered start)
2) Simultaneously start a small fleet of persistent streaming clients (websocket) that open low-latency chat sessions
3) Trigger a controlled proxy rotation on edge-proxy fleet (simulates deployed rotation)
4) Observe transient 429 spikes across streaming connections and some ingestion workers for ~minutes

Observed behavior:
- 429s include X-RateLimit-* headers showing token window exhausted and refill next at epoch aligned to origin window
- Edge proxies report token counters higher than origin by ~1 window (window length 60s), causing immediate rejection until origin refills
- Retry patterns: clients backoff then retry; some health-check probes from rotated proxies generate additional refills and contribute to tokenfanout

Expected behavior:
- Edge and origin should maintain consistent view of token availability after rotation; refill alignment should not cause consumer-level 429s during normal rotations.

Logs / Artifacts:
- Excerpt from edge-proxy logs (edge-proxy-12) at 02:05 UTC: "token_count_local=120, token_count_origin=30, next_refill=2026-03-10T02:05:00Z"
- Rate-limiter traces show abrupt decrement for websocket route /v1/stream/chat after proxy reconnect
- Customer provided application-side retry stats and shortened timeline (attached as support_upload_456789_metrics.zip)

Initial hypothesis:
- Refill window skew between edge caches and central accounting during rotation results in short-lived double-accounting or under-accounting depending on which side refills first.
- Health-checks and warmup traffic from newly rotated proxies cause small token leaks that are attributed to tenant before origin has reconciled.
- Concurrent mixed workload (many long-lived streams + high-parallel batch workers) increases sensitivity to short refill misalignments.

Investigation notes:
- Pulled rate-limiter metrics for dp-us-east-02 between 01:50 and 03:00 UTC; saw spike in handshake and auth requests coincident with rotation window.
- Edge proxies use a 60s refill window; origin uses sliding-refill with clock aligned to NTP. Drift observed on a subset of proxies (0.8s).
- Reproduced locally by simulating proxy restart with staggered cache purge; reproduced transient 429s when both streaming and bulk workers active.

Temporary mitigation (applied 2026-03-10 03:10 UTC):
- Increased edge-local soft-burst allowance by 15% for dp-us-east-02 to allow short burst while origin reconciles.
- Applied short-term client guidance to increase jittered backoff and exponential retry cap for BrightRetail bulk workers (reduce concurrent open workers from 200->100 during next rotation window).

Next steps / Proposed fix:
1) Short-term (low risk): add a 2s grace period after proxy rotation where edge accepts tokens until origin reports final refill state (feature flag rollout).
2) Medium-term: introduce a rotation handshake where rotated proxy fetches origin snapshot and delays applying local refill deltas until confirmed.
3) Long-term: tighten NTP sync checks and add monitoring alert for proxy-origin refill delta > 1s.
4) Postmortem: schedule follow-up runbook update for Dedicated rotations and include recommended client-side concurrency caps.

Customer communication plan:
- Sent initial findings and mitigation steps to BrightRetail on 2026-03-10 04:00 UTC; recommended immediate backoff changes and informed them of feature-flagged grace period rollout.
- Offer a dedicated post-incident Q&A session and assistance reconfiguring scheduled imports to avoid overlap with rotation windows.

Resolution notes:
- Grace-period feature flag rolled to dp-us-east-02 on 2026-03-11 01:20 UTC; no recurrence detected during subsequent rotation (observed over 48h).
- Follow-up runbook entry created: "Dedicated Proxy Rotation - refill reconciliation" (Confluence link provided).
- Customer confirmed restored throughput and acceptable streaming latency on 2026-03-12.

Follow-ups / action items:
- ENG: implement rotation handshake (PR alice/edge/rotation-handshake) - target 2026-04-05
- SRE: alert for refill-delta > 1s - target 2026-03-20
- DX: add guidance to docs for mixing high concurrency batch jobs with low-latency streams under Dedicated pools.

2026-03-10 07:30 - Runtime Team (Dmitri Kozlov): Confirmed edge local counters can present stale view for up to 1s after rotation; health-checks cause temporary token accounting noise. Suggest short grace acceptance window.

2026-03-10 12:45 - Support (Aisha Patel): Applied temporary increase to edge soft-burst for dp-us-east-02 and advised customer to reduce worker concurrency. Customer accepted and observed improvement.
2026-03-11 02:00 - Marco Nguyen: Grace-period feature flag rolled to production for dp-us-east-02. Monitoring for 48h. No new incidents in observed window.

resolution: Applied edge grace-period, reduced short-term soft-burst accounting, and scheduled engineering work to add rotation handshake. Customer confirmed restored behavior. Runbook and docs updated.
workaround: Reduce parallel import workers during known rotation windows; apply jittered backoff on retries; increase client-side retry cap windows temporarily.
